18.t: Working with data: skin and current
q: Which condition gives the lowest resistance?
Skin broken by a cut (500 Ω).
Calculate the current for sweaty hands. Use I = V / R.
A current over about 30 mA can stop the heart. Which conditions are dangerous?
Wet skin (220 mA) and a cut (440 mA); sweaty hands (22 mA) is close to the limit.
Explain why sockets are not allowed near a bath or shower.
Wet skin has very low resistance, so mains voltage would drive a current many times the deadly level. Water also conducts, giving an easy path to earth.
